question: The seamless operation of flights is crucial for the competitiveness and sustainability of tourism-based economies, such as that of Greece. However, delayed flights at Greek airports resulting from air traffic control capacity constraints (due to understaffing, outdated systems) highlight the weaknesses of the Civil Aviation Authority.

Data shows that the nominal capacity (22 arrivals per hour) has been exceeded on numerous occasions, and while commitments have been made to renew critical equipment (radars, communications, navigation systems), the relevant contracts have not been signed.
The problem now has a European dimension, as the failure to meet capacity and availability indicators affects the uniform functioning of the European air navigation network.

It is worth remembering that the current Single European Sky (SES) framework provides for binding targets, a performance and charging scheme and supervision on the basis of Regulation (EU) 2017/373, while EUROCONTROL, as the network manager, has a mandate to balance demand and capacity.
What is more, the SESAR programmes and the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) also provide financial tools to upgrade CNS/radar systems and to provide staff with training. Can the Commission say: 1.
How does it assess Greece’s compliance with its SES obligations and what corrective measures is it considering in this regard?
What direct operational interventions can be implemented by the network manager in order to reduce delays?
How can the absorption of European funding (CEF, SESAR) be sped up to upgrade systems and meet staffing needs?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.3.2026) Greece is partially compliant with EU legislation on Air Traffic Management (ATM)1. Three infringement procedures are open regarding the deployment of datalink capabilities2, the deployment of modern radars3, and the publication of performance-based navigation (PBN) procedures at Greek airports4.

On 11 December 2025, the Commission decided5 to refer Greece to the Court of Justice of the European Union for failing to put in place the necessary measures to design and publish PBN procedures, and to send a reasoned opinion for failing to deploy modern radars. The serious incident resulting in the closure of the Greek airspace on 4 January 2026 underlines the urgency for Greece to modernise its ATM system.

The Commission services are in close contact with the Greek authorities and HASP (the Greek Air Navigation Service Provider) and receive regular progress reports on the status of corrective actions. EUROCONTROL acting as Network Manager in accordance with the Network Functions Implementing Regulation6, is actively taking measures to reduce delays, such as through Air Traffic Flow Management.

These allow adequate management in cases of bad weather, route availability restrictions, lack of capacity in some States, and evolving airspace configurations. Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) funding supports European stakeholders in implementing the requirements of the Single European Sky, provided they adhere to compliance deadlines.

CEF cannot fund actions to comply with EU regulations that are subject to infringement procedures. Furthermore, CEF funding cannot be used to meet staffing needs. The Greek law 5240/2025 aims to grant HASP the autonomy, resources, and capabilities to invest in staff and technology.
